_construction_note: Authored 2026-08-08, Phase 5 tranche 14 (packet L), strictly after documents_batch17.json and after extraction was verified directly -- this case's construction directly triggered discovery and repair of taxonomy #24 (order-dependent `chosen` selection when no document is CURRENT), fixed in the same pass before this case file was finalized. DEVELOPMENT-tainted the moment used below.

cases.query: What is Ironclad Facilities Management's current service tier under CT-2026-6027?

expected_state.temporal_status: Genuinely tricky combined case: the original STANDARD tier was SUPERSEDED by an amendment upgrading to PREMIUM, but that amendment was ITSELF later revoked with no successor amendment issued -- so nothing is currently in force for this predicate. Deterministically resolves to the most recently effective known state (PREMIUM, REVOKED) with STANDARD as the historical predecessor -- found and fixed a real order-dependence bug (taxonomy #24) in the process: which of the two non-current candidates became the committed state used to depend on grounding_document_ids list order before this case was built.
expected_state.correct_summary: Neither STANDARD nor PREMIUM is confidently current -- the amendment that would have made PREMIUM current was itself revoked. A model should hedge here (honest SUMMARY/null -> CONSISTENT); a confident assertion of EITHER tier is TEMPORAL_CONTRADICTION, via the same mechanism in both cases (the committed state's own temporal_status is REVOKED, so any confident value-claim is rejected before the specific asserted value is even compared).

cases.ungoverned_failure_mode: Model confidently asserts either the original STANDARD tier or the revoked PREMIUM upgrade as the settled current state, when the actual situation is unresolved pending renegotiation -- the source document's own words.
